moduleSystem.headline: Swappable diode modules on D1 Pro frame
moduleSystem.description: xTool D1 Pro uses plug-in diode modules (5W–40W depending on era and listing). Buy the module power you need: same rail and software as other D1 Pro heads.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 20W diode module balances engraving and light cutting on xTool D1 Pro: the most versatile SKU before stepping up to a stronger head.
editorialDepth.limitations: If thick cutting dominates your week, compare 40W. Verify which module is in the box: same chassis, different heads.

faq.question: What does the D1 Pro 20W cut in one pass?
faq.answer: xTool rates it for 10 mm basswood plywood and 8 mm solid wood in one pass, and 5 mm acrylic in several opaque colours (black, red, orange, yellow, light green). Denser hardwoods such as beech, cherry and bamboo need several passes.

faq.question: D1 Pro 20W or 40W?
faq.answer: The 20W covers most hobby and Etsy work: plywood boxes, ornaments, dark acrylic. The 40W made sense for regular 10–15 mm cuts and faster batches, but sold at about $999 against $699–$899 for the 20W. With the line discontinued, compare used prices rather than the original gap.

faq.question: Is a used D1 Pro 20W still a good buy?
faq.answer: It was the most popular D1 Pro head, so used units and community settings are easy to find. Check laser output on a test cut (xTool's own test cut a 5 mm basswood square in about one minute at full power), the lens and the frame's squareness. xTool no longer sells the D1 Pro new.

standoutFeatures.title: 10 mm plywood in one pass
standoutFeatures.body: xTool rates the 20W head for 10 mm basswood plywood and 8 mm solid wood in a single pass, which covers most box, sign and ornament work.

standoutFeatures.title: Opaque coloured acrylic
standoutFeatures.body: xTool's tests show 5 mm acrylic cut in one pass in black, red, orange, yellow and light green, not only black.
